verified_findings: cargo vendor is documented to vendor crates.io and git dependencies into a specified local directory containing the remote dependency sources.

After vendoring, Cargo prints the configuration necessary to use the vendored sources to stdout; the documentation says it must be added or redirected to Cargo configuration, usually .cargo/config.toml for the current package.
Cargo treats vendored sources as read-only, like registry and git sources.

The --respect-source-config option affects which configured sources are read while downloading crates; the documented vendoring operation itself therefore remains a dependency-materialization/download step rather than a pure metadata rewrite.
slice.phase1_interpretation: The documentation supports a zero-network steady-state pattern only after dependency sources have already been materialized and the corresponding Cargo source configuration has been installed. It does not establish a scheduled-Chat-native way to perform the initial cargo vendor process. Therefore initial vendoring/execution remains an unresolved child unless a repository already contains the vendored tree and compatible config.
